description: Xor keeps the steps of an explanation whose node another explanation does not select, then the steps of that explanation whose node the first does not select, in its order
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * quantity
tax = subtotal * rate
shipping = quantity * 2
total = subtotal + tax
freight = shipping + rate
(why total |> xor(why freight)).map(step -> step.node)

description: Swapping the two explanations begins the symmetric difference with the other's own steps, over the same nodes
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * quantity
tax = subtotal * rate
shipping = quantity * 2
total = subtotal + tax
freight = shipping + rate
[(why freight |> xor(why total)).map(step -> step.node), (why total |> xor(why freight)).length]

description: A symmetric difference of two impact selections lists what a change of exactly one of the two inputs reaches
code:
price = 10
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * 3
tax = subtotal * rate
total = subtotal + tax
fee = rate * 5
(affects price |> xor(affects rate)).map(step -> step.node)

description: A state filter after xor keeps the facts that tell two explanations apart
code:
fan = 2
load = 40
speed = 3
current = load * 2
heat = current + fan
noise = fan * speed
(why heat |> xor(why noise) |> stated).map(step -> step.node)

description: A depth stage after xor measures each side from where its own walk began, which differs from the symmetric difference of the two limited walks
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
d = a + 3
[(why c |> xor(why d) |> depth(1)).map(step -> step.node), (why c |> depth(1) |> xor(why d |> depth(1))).map(step -> step.node)]

description: A walk after xor starts from every step that the symmetric difference keeps
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
d = a + 3
f = d + 1
(b |> xor(d) |> affects).map(step -> step.node)

description: A standing symmetric difference follows a rewiring that moves a node into both explanations
code:
a = 1
b = 2
left = a + b
right = b + 1
apart = why left |> xor(why right)
right = a + b + 1
apart.map(step -> step.node)

description: Xor with model selects the other nodes of the model in model order, and the symmetric difference of a selection with itself is empty
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = 4
[(why b |> xor(model)).map(step -> step.node), (why b |> xor(why b)).length]

description: A name that holds a selection is a reasoning observer, so as the other selection it selects nothing; the pipeline is written in place
code:
price = 10
tax = price * 2
shipping = price + 1
causes = why shipping
[(why tax |> xor(causes)).map(step -> step.node), (why tax |> xor(why shipping)).map(step -> step.node)]

description: A class-level rule gives every instance its own symmetric difference
code:
class Item(price, qty, fee):
    this.price = price
    this.qty = qty
    this.fee = fee
$Item.total = $Item.price * $Item.qty
$Item.cost = $Item.qty + $Item.fee
$Item.apart = why $Item.total |> xor(why $Item.cost)
pen = Item(2, 5, 1)
cup = Item(3, 1, 4)
[pen.apart.map(step -> step.node), cup.apart.map(step -> step.node)]

description: Nodes names the steps of a symmetric difference, and an other selection that a depth with a null limit makes undefined makes it undefined
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
d = a + 3
n = null
[c |> why |> xor(d |> why) |> nodes, c |> why |> xor(d |> why |> depth(n))]

description: A binding named xor shadows the stage when the pipeline runs, so a try statement can catch the error
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
xor = 0
result = ""
try:
    result = why b |> xor(why a)
catch error:
    result = error
[xor, result]
